title: Genesis Chapter 46 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 46 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 46 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 46.

questions.question: Where did Israel offer sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac before his journey?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:1 states that Israel came to Beersheba and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac.

questions.question: How did God speak to Israel in Genesis 46?
options: In the visions of the night
questions.correctAnswer: In the visions of the night
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:2 records that God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night.

questions.question: What did God tell Jacob not to fear in Genesis 46?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:3 says God told Jacob not to fear to go down into Egypt.

questions.question: Who did God say would put his hand upon Jacob's eyes?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:4 states that Joseph shall put his hand upon Jacob's eyes.

questions.question: What means of transport did Pharaoh send to carry Jacob and his family?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:5 says the sons of Israel carried Jacob and their families in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent.

questions.question: Besides Jacob, who went with him into Egypt according to Genesis 46?
options: His sons, daughters, and all his seed
questions.correctAnswer: His sons, daughters, and all his seed
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:7 states that Jacob brought his sons, sons' sons, daughters, sons' daughters, and all his seed into Egypt.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn son of Jacob?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:8 identifies Reuben as Jacob's firstborn.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a son of Reuben?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:9 lists Hanoch, Phallu, Hezron, and Carmi as sons of Reuben. Jemuel was a son of Simeon.

questions.question: How many sons of Simeon are named in Genesis 46?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:10 names six sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a son of Levi?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:11 states the sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Pharez was a son of Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Er and Onan, sons of Judah, died in the land of Canaan.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:12 specifies that Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob's family brought only their goods into Egypt, but left their cattle behind.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:6 states they took their cattle and their goods into Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to go down with Jacob into Egypt and also to bring him up again.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:4 records God's promise to go down with Jacob into Egypt and bring him up again.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph was the only son of Rachel mentioned in Genesis 46.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:19 mentions both Joseph and Benjamin as sons of Rachel.

questions.question: In Genesis 46, which event happens first?
options: God speaks to Jacob in visions
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:1 shows Jacob offering sacrifices at Beersheba before God speaks to him in visions (verse 2) and the later events.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 46 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 46 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 46:13, who were the sons of Issachar?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:13 specifically lists the sons of Issachar as Tola, Phuvah, Job, and Shimron, distinguishing them from other tribes and their descendants mentioned in nearby verses.

questions.question: What does Genesis 46:14 tell us about the sons of Zebulun?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 names the sons of Zebulun as Sered, Elon, and Jahleel, highlighting the importance of genealogical records in understanding Israel's family structure.

questions.question: How many souls did Leah bear unto Jacob in Padanaram, including his daughter Dinah, according to Genesis 46:15?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:15 states that Leah bore thirty-three souls to Jacob, including his sons and daughters, emphasizing the large family God blessed Jacob with through Leah.

questions.question: Which sons belonged to Gad as listed in Genesis 46:16?
options: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli
Belah, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman
Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul
questions.correctAnswer: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly lists these seven as the sons of Gad, showing the continuation of Jacob's lineage through his sons.

questions.question: According to Genesis 46:17, who were the sons of Asher and who was their sister?
options: Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui, Beriah, and Serah their sister
questions.correctAnswer: Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui, Beriah, and Serah their sister
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:17 identifies the sons of Asher and includes their sister Serah, highlighting the presence of female family members alongside males in the lineage.

questions.question: What lesson about God's providence and blessing can be drawn from Genesis 46:18 which lists the sons of Zilpah?
options: God blesses and multiplies families even through secondary wives
Only the firstborn sons receive God's blessing
Genealogies are unimportant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses and multiplies families even through secondary wives
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:18 shows that Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, bore sixteen souls to Jacob, illustrating that God's blessing extends beyond primary wives to include all family members.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Rachel, according to Genesis 46:19 and 46:22?
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 22 identify Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel, emphasizing Rachel’s unique role among Jacob’s wives.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 46:20, who were the sons of Joseph, and what does this teach us about God's blessings?
options: Manasseh and Ephraim; God blesses children born even in foreign lands
Belah and Becher; God only blesses those born in Canaan
Hezron and Hamul; God blesses only sons of Leah
Hushim and Jahzeel; God limits blessings to Israel's direct land
questions.correctAnswer: Manasseh and Ephraim; God blesses children born even in foreign lands
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:20 describes Joseph’s sons born in Egypt, showing God's continued blessings regardless of location, supporting trust in God's providence in all circumstances.

questions.question: According to Genesis 46:21, which names are listed as sons of Benjamin?
options: Belah, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard
Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli
Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul
questions.correctAnswer: Belah, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:21 provides a detailed list of Benjamin's sons, demonstrating the importance of family lines and God's provision for each tribe.

questions.question: How does Genesis 46:23 describe the sons of Dan, and what can this teach about God's diversity in blessing?
options: Dan had only one son, Hushim, showing that God's plans vary for each family
Dan had many sons, demonstrating abundant blessing
Dan had no sons mentioned, indicating disfavor
Dan's sons were the greatest warriors
questions.correctAnswer: Dan had only one son, Hushim, showing that God's plans vary for each family
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states Dan's sole son was Hushim, teaching that God's blessings and plans differ and that faithfulness is not measured by quantity but by God's purpose.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Naphtali as listed in Genesis 46:24?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:24 names these four as the sons of Naphtali, completing the genealogical record and showing God's faithfulness to each tribe.

questions.question: What does Genesis 46:15 teach about the importance of recognizing family members in God's plan?
questions.explanation: The verse counts both sons and daughters (including Dinah), emphasizing that all family members, male and female, are significant in God's covenant and blessings.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 46:18, Zilpah was Rachel's handmaid.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:18 clearly states Zilpah was given to Leah by Laban as her handmaid, not Rachel's, indicating an important distinction in family relationships.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 46:22 shows that the total number of souls born to Rachel that came to Egypt was fourteen.
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explicitly states the total souls of Rachel's children were fourteen, demonstrating careful record-keeping of God's people.

questions.question: Considering Genesis 46:15 and 46:18, what does the difference in the number of souls born to Leah and Zilpah teach us about God's blessings and family?
options: God blesses families differently but all contribute to His plan
Only Leah's children are significant in God's covenant
Zilpah's children were not counted among Israel
The number of children determines God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses families differently but all contribute to His plan
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 18 show Leah bore 33 souls and Zilpah 16, teaching that God's blessings vary but every family member is vital in His covenant and purpose.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 46 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 46.

questions.question: How many total souls of Jacob's household came into Egypt, including the sons of Joseph born in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:27 states that all the souls of the house of Jacob which came into Egypt were seventy, including Joseph's two sons born in Egypt.

questions.question: Who did Jacob send before him to Joseph to direct him to Goshen?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:28 clearly mentions that Jacob sent Judah before him unto Joseph to direct his face unto Goshen.

questions.question: What was Joseph's reaction when he met his father Israel in Goshen?
options: He wept on his neck a good while
He immediately introduced him to Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: He wept on his neck a good while
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:29 records that Joseph fell on Israel's neck and wept on his neck a good while, showing deep emotional reunion.

questions.question: What did Israel say to Joseph after seeing his face alive?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:30 quotes Israel saying, 'Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive,' expressing fulfillment and peace.

questions.question: What occupation did Joseph tell his brethren to claim before Pharaoh to ensure they could dwell in Goshen?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:32 and 46:34 instruct Joseph's brethren to say their trade is shepherding, as shepherds are abomination to Egyptians and thus allowed to live in Goshen.

questions.question: Why were Joseph's brethren advised to say their occupation was shepherding when questioned by Pharaoh?
options: Because shepherds were respected in Egypt
Because Pharaoh was a shepherd himself
Because every shepherd was an abomination to the Egyptians
Because they wanted to hide their true profession
questions.correctAnswer: Because every shepherd was an abomination to the Egyptians
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:34 states that every shepherd was an abomination unto the Egyptians; this cultural disdain allowed Jacob's family to dwell separately in Goshen.

questions.question: How many souls did the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid, number when they came to Egypt?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:25 specifies that the sons of Bilhah who came to Egypt numbered seven souls.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'souls' (נֶפֶשׁ, nephesh) generally signify in the context of Genesis 46?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'nephesh' used in Genesis 46:26 refers broadly to persons or living beings, indicating the count of individuals in Jacob's family.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Genesis 46 to emphasize the completeness of Jacob's family entering Egypt?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46 uses inclusio by listing the sons and grandsons at the beginning (verses 8-25) and then summarizing total souls at the end (verses 26-27), framing the family's arrival.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God promising to multiply a great nation as in Genesis 46's vision to Jacob?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:3 features God's promise to make a great nation, echoing the original Abrahamic covenant in Genesis 12:2 where God promises to make Abraham a great nation.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects on Joseph's role as a type of Christ, foreshadowed in his care for Jacob and family in Egypt as in Genesis 46?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:22 references Joseph's faith in God's promises and his actions toward his family, typifying Christ's redemptive work, as seen in Genesis 46:4-5.

questions.question: What cultural significance does the fear of shepherds by Egyptians, as mentioned in Genesis 46:34, have in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: Shepherds were associated with foreign nomads and thus despised
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherds were associated with foreign nomads and thus despised
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:34 reveals Egyptian disdain for shepherds, reflecting historical attitudes toward nomadic pastoralists as culturally and ritually impure outsiders in the ancient Near East.

questions.question: According to Genesis 46:31, what was Joseph's intention in going up to Pharaoh regarding his family?
options: To ask for land in Goshen
To request food for his family
To inform Pharaoh that his brethren and father's house from Canaan had come to him
To introduce Israel as a new ruler
questions.correctAnswer: To inform Pharaoh that his brethren and father's house from Canaan had come to him
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:31 records Joseph's plan to tell Pharaoh that his family from Canaan had arrived, preparing for their settlement in Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 46:26, the total number of Jacob's family members who came into Egypt, including wives, was sixty-six.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:26 clarifies that excluding the sons' wives, the total number was sixty-six; thus including wives, the number was higher as stated in verse 27.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 46 records that Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, were born to him in Egypt by Asenath, daughter of Potipherah.
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:20 explicitly states that Joseph's sons Manasseh and Ephraim were born in Egypt to Asenath, daughter of Potipherah.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 46 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 46 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is revealed in God's reassurance to Jacob about going down into Egypt?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:3 reveals God's providence as He promises to make Jacob a great nation in Egypt and to be with him there, showing God's sovereign care over the unfolding plan of salvation.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by God's promise to 'bring thee up again' from Egypt?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:4 indicates God's promise to bring Jacob up again from Egypt, foreshadowing the doctrine of resurrection and God's power over death, which aligns with later biblical teaching on bodily resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:21).

questions.question: What theological significance is found in the fact that Jacob and all his family came into Egypt with their cattle and goods?
options: It signifies God's blessing on their material wealth
It shows their idolatry with possessions
It represents their separation from God's covenant
It denotes their dependence on Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God's blessing on their material wealth
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:6 demonstrates God's blessing and provision as Jacob's entire family moves with their possessions, indicating God's faithfulness in sustaining His covenant people materially.

questions.question: How does the sending of wagons by Pharaoh to carry Jacob and his family demonstrate God's providential care?
options: It illustrates God's direct intervention on behalf of His people
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's direct intervention on behalf of His people
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:5 shows that Pharaoh sent wagons to carry Jacob’s family, which indicates God’s providential orchestration in preparing for His covenant people’s preservation and future blessing (cf. Exodus 3:21-22).

questions.question: What does the detailed listing of Jacob's descendants in Genesis 46 teach about God's covenant faithfulness?
options: It emphasizes human genealogy over divine promise
It underscores God's faithfulness to His covenant promises through generations
It shows the importance of tribal warfare
It highlights the failure of some descendants
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores God's faithfulness to His covenant promises through generations
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:7 and the following verses list Jacob’s family, affirming God’s faithfulness to multiply Abraham’s seed as promised (Genesis 12:2), showing the continuation of the covenant line.

questions.question: What doctrine is exemplified by Joseph's role in comforting Jacob and the promise that he will 'put his hand upon thine eyes'?
options: The doctrine of Christ as the comforter
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of Christ as the comforter
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:4 portrays Joseph as a type of Christ, who comforts Jacob in his dying moments, prefiguring Christ’s role as the ultimate comforter and reconciler (John 14:16).

questions.question: How does Genesis 46:28-30 reflect the theme of restoration in the biblical narrative?
options: It shows the restoration of Israel's land possession
It portrays the emotional restoration of the family unity
It depicts the restoration of political power
It indicates a restoration of temple worship
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the emotional restoration of the family unity
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:29-30 shows Joseph meeting his father and the emotional reunion, symbolizing God's restoration of the family covenant and foreshadowing the ultimate restoration of God's people (Ephesians 2:14-16).

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's sovereignty and human obedience is found in Genesis 46:1-2 and Genesis 46:33-34?
options: God controls all events, but human obedience is irrelevant
Human obedience is required, but God is not sovereign
God sovereignly directs His people, who must obediently present themselves rightly in foreign lands
God forces His people to comply politically
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs His people, who must obediently present themselves rightly in foreign lands
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:1-2 shows God speaking to Jacob guiding him to Egypt, and 46:33-34 shows instructions for the family’s conduct before Pharaoh, teaching God's sovereignty over events alongside the call to faithful obedience (Romans 13:1).

questions.question: What theological significance does the presence of the Canaanite woman Shaul among Simeon's sons have in this chapter's context?
options: It shows God's approval of intermarriage with pagans
It highlights the reality of sin and human failure even within God's covenant family
It demonstrates ethnic purity in Israel
It indicates that Simeon was not part of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the reality of sin and human failure even within God's covenant family
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:10 mentions Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman, illustrating that human sin and failure coexist even among God's chosen, pointing to the need for salvation (Romans 7:18).

questions.question: How does the enumeration of the total number of Jacob's family members (Genesis 46:26-27) reflect God's faithfulness to the Abrahamic covenant?
options: It shows God's failure to multiply the seed
It confirms God’s promise to make Abraham’s descendants numerous
It indicates that only a few survived
It suggests a loss of God's blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms God’s promise to make Abraham’s descendants numerous
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:26-27 counts seventy souls, fulfilling God's covenant promise to Abraham that his descendants would become a great nation (Genesis 12:2).

questions.question: What does the instruction given in Genesis 46:34 about shepherds being abominable to the Egyptians reveal about Israel’s distinctiveness?
options: Israel was to assimilate Egyptian culture
Israel was to embrace Egyptian religion
Israel was to maintain a distinct identity as shepherds, separated from Egyptian customs
Israel would abandon their pastoral lifestyle
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was to maintain a distinct identity as shepherds, separated from Egyptian customs
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:34 commands the Israelites to present themselves as shepherds, a trade abhorred by Egyptians, emphasizing their distinctiveness and God’s preservation of their identity (Exodus 3:12).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is emphasized by His appearing to Jacob 'in the visions of the night' to speak reassurance?
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:2 shows God communicating directly with Jacob in a vision, reflecting God's immanence—His closeness and active involvement with His people (Psalm 139:7-10).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's promise to bring Jacob 'up again' from Egypt is merely a human wish without divine guarantee. What does Genesis 46:4 actually teach about this promise?
options: It is a conditional promise depending on Jacob's faith
It is a sovereign and certain promise from God, demonstrating His power to preserve and redeem
It is symbolic with no real fulfillment
It is a promise only to Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: It is a sovereign and certain promise from God, demonstrating His power to preserve and redeem
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:4 records God’s explicit promise to bring Jacob up again, assuring the covenant’s continuation and prefiguring Israel’s exodus, affirming God's sovereign power to fulfill His word (Exodus 3:12).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God’s covenant and human family does the listing of the sons of Leah (Genesis 46:8-15) and the sons of Rachel (Genesis 46:19-22) provide?
options: God’s covenant is limited to Leah’s descendants only
God’s covenant includes all of Jacob’s descendants, emphasizing both election and human family dynamics
Rachel’s sons were excluded from the covenant
Only the firstborn sons are part of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant includes all of Jacob’s descendants, emphasizing both election and human family dynamics
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:8-15 and 19-22 show that both Leah’s and Rachel’s sons are enumerated among the covenant family, underscoring God’s inclusive covenant faithfulness and the complexity of human family relationships within divine election (Romans 9:6-8).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does the sending of Judah before Joseph to Goshen (Genesis 46:28) have with the broader redemption story?
options: It foreshadows the tribal leadership in Israel and God's orderly plan for His people’s settlement
It illustrates Judah’s rejection by Joseph
It signifies a break in the covenant
It marks the end of Israel’s identity
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the tribal leadership in Israel and God's orderly plan for His people’s settlement
questions.explanation: Genesis 46:28 shows Judah sent ahead, indicating his emerging leadership role, which connects to the Messianic line and God’s sovereign ordering of Israel’s history (Genesis 49:10).
